item.title: 1984: Four Days After His 20th Birthday
item.description: Four days after his 20th birthday, New York Mets pitcher Dwight Gooden becomes the youngest player ever to win the National League Rookie of the Year Award. Gooden posted a 17–9 (2.60) record, with a major league-leading 276 strikeouts. He captures 23 of 24 first-place votes. Photo: Barry Colla Photography (Public domain).

item.title: 2014: MLB Commissioner Bud Selig Announce That Baseball Team Owners
item.description: MLB Commissioner Bud Selig announce that baseball team owners unanimously approved a five-year term for Rob Manfred, who will succeed the longtime commissioner early next year. Manfred has worked for MLB since 1998, and was chosen to replace Selig in past August over Boston Red Sox chairman Tom Werner. Photo: Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff on Flickr (Original version) (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2013: The Tigers Traded Prince Fielder to the Texas Rangers for Three Time
item.description: On November 20, 2013, the Tigers traded Prince Fielder to the Texas Rangers for three time All-Star second baseman Ian Kinsler plus cash considerations with regard to Fielder's remaining contract amount. Photo: Dave Hogg from Royal Oak, MI, USA (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2010: Bailey Signed a Minor League Contract With the Minnesota Twins
item.description: On November 20, 2010, Bailey signed a minor league contract with the Minnesota Twins with an invitation to spring training. Photo: Keith Allison on Flickr (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2010: The Notre Dame Fighting Irish Played a College Football Game
item.description: The Notre Dame Fighting Irish played a college football game at Yankee Stadium against The Army Black Knights on November 20, 2010, with the Irish defeating the Black Knights 27–3. Photo: Matt Boulton (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2007: Estrada Was Traded From the Brewers to the New York Mets for Pitcher
item.description: On November 20, 2007, Estrada was traded from the Brewers to the New York Mets for pitcher Guillermo Mota. Photo: User Chrisjnelson on en.wikipedia (CC BY 3.0).

item.title: 2007: Philadelphia Phillies Shortstop Jimmy Rollins Wins the NL Most
item.description: Philadelphia Phillies shortstop Jimmy Rollins wins the NL Most Valuable Player Award. Photo: Keith Allison (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 1990: Oakland Athletics Outfielder Rickey Henderson Was Named American
item.description: Oakland Athletics outfielder Rickey Henderson was named American League MVP. Photo: User Dlz28 on en.wikipedia (Public domain).

item.title: 1982: Bob Short, 65, Baseball and Basketball Club Owner
item.description: Bob Short, 65, baseball and basketball club owner; bought expansion Washington Senators on December 3, 1968, moved them to Arlington, Texas, as the Texas Rangers after the 1971 season, then sold franchise to Brad Corbett on May 29, 1974; earlier, he owned the NBA's Minneapolis Lakers and moved them to Los Angeles in 1960, selling them to Jack Kent Cooke in 1965. Photo: Robert L. Knudsen, White House photographer. (Public domain).

item.title: 1981: In a Five-Player, Three-Team Trade
item.description: In a five-player, three-team trade, the Cleveland Indians send catcher Bo Díaz to the Philadelphia Phillies; the Phillies deal outfielder Lonnie Smith to the St. Louis Cardinals; the Cardinals trade pitchers Silvio Martinez and Lary Sorensen to the Indians, and the Phillies send Cleveland a player to be named later (pitcher Scott Munninghoff) to complete the transaction. Photo: Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 1978: Warren Brown, 84, Chicago Sportswriter
item.description: Warren Brown, 84, Chicago sportswriter, who earned J. G. Taylor Spink Award honors in 1973, and was inducted in the National Baseball Hall of Fame the same year along with outfielder Mickey Mantle, pitcher Whitey Ford and umpire Jocko Conlan Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1975: The Financially Struggling San Francisco Giants
item.description: The financially struggling San Francisco Giants, who finished third in the National League West and drew only 522,919 fans to Candlestick Park in 1975 (worst in MLB), fire manager Wes Westrum. They will not name a replacement until March 3, 1976, after the team has been sold by Horace Stoneham to Bob Lurie and Arthur "Bud" Herseth, when they coax former Giant skipper Bill Rigney out of retirement.

item.title: 1974: Texas Rangers Right Fielder Jeff Burroughs, Who Batted .301
item.description: Texas Rangers right fielder Jeff Burroughs, who batted .301 with 25 home runs and a league-leading 118 RBI, wins the American League MVP Award. Oakland teammates Joe Rudi, Sal Bando and Reggie Jackson are the runners-up. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1972: Future Baseball Hall of Fame Catcher Carlton Fisk of the Boston Red
item.description: Future Baseball Hall of Fame catcher Carlton Fisk of the Boston Red Sox (All-Star, Gold Glove Award, 22 HR, 61 RBI, .293) is the unanimous winner of the American League Rookie of the Year Award. The following day, New York Mets left-hander Jon Matlack (15–10, 2.32 ERA), wins 1972's NL "ROTY" honor, receiving 19 of 24 votes. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1969: Willie McCovey of the San Francisco Giants Is Voted National League
item.description: Willie McCovey of the San Francisco Giants is voted National League Most Valuable Player after he led the league with 45 home runs, 126 RBI, and a .453 on-base percentage and .656 slugging percentage. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1968: Al Campanis Succeeds the Late Fresco Thompson
item.description: Al Campanis succeeds the late Fresco Thompson as head of baseball operations of the Los Angeles Dodgers. His official title is vice president, player personnel, but Campanis will function as the team's general manager until April 1987. Photo: Cal Montney, Los Angeles Times (CC BY 4.0).

item.title: 1960: With the American League Expansion Draft Less Than Four Weeks Away
item.description: With the American League expansion draft less than four weeks away, Quesada's "new" Senators appoint former American Association president Ed Doherty, 60, general manager, and former first baseman, two-time batting champion and star of the "old" Senators Mickey Vernon, 42, the expansion team's field manager. Photo: Wikimedia Commons (Public domain).

item.title: 1960: A Play Known Simply as The Hit Occurred at Yankee Stadium on November
item.description: A play known simply as The Hit occurred at Yankee Stadium on November 20, 1960. Photo: Severin St. Martin (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 1958: The Detroit Tigers Trade Pitcher Al Cicotte
item.description: The Detroit Tigers trade pitcher Al Cicotte and second baseman Billy Martin to the Cleveland Indians for hurlers Don Mossi and Ray Narleski and infielder Ossie Álvarez. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1952: Fred McMullin, Best Known for His Involvement in the 1919 World
item.description: Fred McMullin, best known for his involvement in the 1919 World Series Black Sox Scandal, died in Los Angeles, California, at the age of 61. McMullin, a reserve infielder with the Chicago White Sox, was one of the eight White Sox players that were banned from baseball for gambling on the series, won by the Cincinnati Reds. Photo: Underwood & Underwood (Public domain).

item.title: 1952: Hank Sauer, Slugging Outfielder of the Chicago Cubs Who Is Nicknamed
item.description: Hank Sauer, slugging outfielder of the Chicago Cubs who is nicknamed "The Mayor of Wrigley Field," wins the 1952 National League Most Valuable Player Award. Sauer, 35, tied Ralph Kiner for the Senior Circuit's home-run crown, with 37 blasts, and led the NL in RBI (121). Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1947: Kokos Was Originally a Cleveland Indians Prospect
item.description: Kokos was originally a Cleveland Indians prospect, and was traded on November 20, 1947 with $25,000, Joe Frazier, and Bryan Stephens for Walt Judnich and Bob Muncrief. Photo: Unknown (Public domain).

item.title: 1947: Boston Braves Third Baseman Bob Elliott Is Selected 1947's National
item.description: Boston Braves third baseman Bob Elliott is selected 1947's National League Most Valuable Player by the Baseball Writers' Association of America. Pitcher Ewell Blackwell of the Cincinnati Reds is the runner-up by 30 points. Photo: Bowman Gum (Public domain).

item.title: 1930: William B. Hanna, 68, Sportswriter for Various New York Newspapers
item.description: William B. Hanna, 68, sportswriter for various New York newspapers since 1888, known for his florid writing style.

item.title: 1888: The Joint Rules Committee Reduces the Number of Balls Needed
item.description: The Joint Rules Committee reduces the number of balls needed for a walk to 4. With the 4 ball, 3 strike at-bat and overhand pitching rules now in place, baseball in 1889 will be played very similar to the game of today.

item.title: 1884: The National League Votes to Allow Overhand Pitching for the 1885
item.description: The National League votes to allow overhand pitching for the 1885 season, although there are restrictions placed on the delivery in order to keep velocity down. In addition, teams are now required to supply a separate bench for each club at their park to limit inter-team fraternization. Photo: Betz, John Jr (Public domain).

item.title: 1877: The New York Clipper Sporting Periodical Published a List
item.description: The New York Clipper sporting periodical published a list of the results of interleague competition between the teams of the National League and the teams of the New England Association. The NEA teams win the 48-game competition against the NL teams with 24 victories, 23 defeats and 1 tied contest.
